lead.s: Oncopathology MCQs: Test Your Knowledge on Cancer Pathology — MCQ Bank

b: Produced by: Aspergillus flavus (most common), A. parasiticus , A. pseudotamarii , A. nomius
Affected crops: Corn, peanuts, tobacco, oilseeds, dried fruits, cotton seeds, rice, pepper
B1, B2 — blue fluorescence under UV light (cyclopentane E-ring)
G1, G2 — green fluorescence under UV light (xanthone ring)
M1 — hydroxylated metabolite of AFB1; found in milk, urine and tissues of animals fed contaminated feed; ~10 times less toxic than AFB1

qs.q: Why are aflatoxins considered a significant global public health concern in food safety?
o: They act as potent hepatocarcinogens in humans
They cause acute muscle paralysis upon ingestion
They are poisonous mushrooms mistaken for edibles
They are secondary bacterial metabolites found in dairy
qs.e: Aflatoxins are potent hepatocarcinogens produced by specific Aspergillus species, contaminating foodstuffs like peanuts and grains. They do not cause muscle paralysis or originate from poisonous mushrooms.

qs.q: Aflatoxin, a potent natural hepatocarcinogen, is produced by which fungal species?
qs.e: Aspergillus flavus produces aflatoxin, which is a potent hepatocarcinogen found in contaminated food sources. Other Aspergillus species produce different mycotoxins or clinical syndromes.
qs.s: Medical Mycology Q&A: Fungal Pathogens, Drugs, & Diseases: MCQs

qs.q: Which detoxification method is specifically used in grain management to prevent aflatoxin production by treating the grain with an alkaline chemical for 10 to 14 days?
qs.e: Grain can be treated with anhydrous ammonia for 10–14 days as a mould inhibitor and prevention strategy against aflatoxins. Hydrated sodium calcium aluminosilicate is used as an adsorbent rather than an ammonia-based grain treatment.
qs.s: Mycotoxins & Aflatoxins: Health Risks, Diagnosis & Management: MCQs

qs.q: Which of the following is a recommended treatment to prevent aflatoxin absorption in animals?
qs.e: Cholestyramine binds aflatoxin in the gut, and phenylalanine also reduces absorption. Vitamin C alone is not a specific binder.
qs.s: Mycotoxins & Aflatoxins: Health Risks, Diagnosis & Management: MCQs

qs.q: Aflatoxin is produced by which organism, and what type of substance is it?
qs.e: Aspergillus flavus produces aflatoxin, a mycotoxin known for its potent hepatocarcinogenic properties.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - October 9, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Aflatoxin, a potent hepatocarcinogen, is primarily produced by which organism?
qs.e: Aspergillus flavus is well-known for producing aflatoxin, a mycotoxin that can contaminate nuts and grains and is a significant risk factor for hepatocellular carcinoma.
qs.s: Weekly Year 3: Medical Mycology Exam - August 14, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: Aflatoxins are a serious problem because
o: People often ingest them by mistaking the mushroom for an edible one
They are produced as a byproduct by Aspergillus niger
They contaminate foodstuffs like peanuts and cottonseed oil
qs.e: Aflatoxins are potent hepatocarcinogens, which makes them a significant global public health concern.

qs.q: Aflatoxins are produced by which fungus?
qs.e: Aflatoxins are produced by Aspergillus parasiticus and Aspergillus flavus.
